case_name: Ashok Kumar Chatterjee v State of Madhya Pradesh
respondent:
State of Madhya Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

2  May  1989
Cr.A. No. 417 of 1978 (From the Judgment and Dt. 7 May 1977 of the Madhya Pradesh High Court in Cr.A. No. 307 of 1977)
The Judgment was delivered by: RATNAVEL PANDIAN, J.
1.  This appeal under special leave is directed against the judgment passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Jabalpur disposing Criminal Reference No. 1 of 1977 submitted by the learned Sessions Judge, Raipur u/s. 366(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code for confirmation of the sentence of death awarded by him in Session Trial No. 5 of 1977 and the criminal Appeal No. 307 of 1977 preferred by the appellant, Ashok Kumar Chatterjee challenging the correctness and legality of the judgment made by the trial court convicting him u/s. 302 and 201 IPC and sentencing him to death and to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 3 years respectively.

2.   The deceased Ravindra, who was 19 years o
facts: The deceased Ravindra, a 19-year-old student, was murdered by his cousin Ashok Kumar Chatterjee.
Pritosh Kumar Chatterjee, the father of Ravindra, had an abnormal sexual relationship with his own daughter Supriya.
Ashok Kumar Chatterjee confessed to the police that he had murdered Ravindra and surrendered himself.
Pritosh committed suicide after his wife lodged a complaint with the police.
issues: Whether the appellant's confession was voluntary and admissible in evidence?
Whether the prosecution proved its case beyond reasonable doubt?
court_reasoning: The court held that the appellant's confession was voluntary and admissible in evidence.
The court found that the prosecution had proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.
holding: The Supreme Court upheld the conviction of Ashok Kumar Chatterjee for the murder of Ravindra and sentenced him to death.
